<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ccb058c416b08d4739591c7b95517e6bdc8dda8e` — the merge of head `64b6470c962a6d8c5c45f49d4a9fefcb0c7f3a8c` into base `275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ccb058c416b08d4739591c7b95517e6bdc8dda8e && git checkout ccb058c416b08d4739591c7b95517e6bdc8dda8e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02 64b6470c962a6d8c5c45f49d4a9fefcb0c7f3a8c && git checkout -B drift-repro 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02 && git merge --no-ff 64b6470c962a6d8c5c45f49d4a9fefcb0c7f3a8c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `64b6470c962a6d8c5c45f49d4a9fefcb0c7f3a8c`
Local-runs: probe — `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` `readClause2Line` was run offline over the PR body's own `Clause-②:` line, to settle whether its `(narrowing: …)` spelling reads as the narrowing arm (it does: `declared / no / narrowing`); nothing on the head was built, tested or re-gated, and no worktree was cut.

Inputs read: card #23010 (body and all 4 comments, the objectui pointer `6123054064` included), PR #23076 (body, 10-file list, the net diff `c5b43b606…64b6470c9` read from git objects), the check-runs on the head, and objectui `packages/core/src/actions/navigationTarget.ts` read from git objects at the pinned `7578323a54` and at `origin/main` `5dcb101c93` (byte-identical).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`ActionSchema.target` under `type: 'url'` — accept set narrowed to the runner's closed set. Right.** `navigationTargetRefusal` was read rule by rule against objectui `classifyNavigationTarget`: tab / LF / CR anywhere refused first; `./…` admitted; `/…` admitted unless its second character is `/` or a backslash; `^https?://` and `^mailto:` admitted case-insensitively (the table lookup lowercases the scheme, and `http`/`https` require the `//`); every other scheme and every bare relative (`thanks`, `../thanks`, `?tab=2`, `#top`, a leading space) refused. For every literal target the two functions give the same answer; the test's section 3 replays the runner's own pinned cases. The `.objectui-sha` at the head is `7578323…`, the sha the predicate's docblock cites.
2. **The door exceeds the card's literal scheme clause — refusing `http:host` (no `//`), `/` plus backslash, control characters and bare relatives. Right.** The card body's literal text only refuses scheme-bearing targets and `//host`, so it would have admitted `http:example.com` and `thanks`; both are targets the runner refuses at the click, which is exactly the publish-clean, fail-at-click trap ruling A+ closes. The card's governing principle (one set, stated in the contract, the runtime fulfils exactly that), the thread pointer `6123054064` (read on the claim, `Thread-read:`), and the fork-clause measurement (no non-test producer in either repository writes a refused target; one spec test fixture retriaged) all direct the stricter set. Declared in the PR body, the changeset's FROM → TO table and the D3 entry.
3. **`InlineActionSchema` door, legacy `type: 'navigation'` + `to` included. Right.** The `superRefine` is chained after `z.preprocess(normalizeInlineAction, …)` and after the target-required refine, so the legacy spelling is folded onto `url` + `target` before it is judged, and the issue lands at `['target']`. `element:button`'s `action` inherits it (pinned on `ElementButtonPropsSchema`).
4. **A target opening with `${` is deferred to the click. Right — the card orders it.** `${ctx.url}`, `${param.url}/details`, `${ctx.origin}/x` pass; a template that opens elsewhere (`/x?id=${param.id}`, `mailto:${param.email}`) is judged on its literal head, which is what the runner does after interpolation. Residual, named not flagged: a `${`-headed template that interpolates to a refused value, or carries a control character, is refused only at the click — that is the card's own deferral.
5. **Empty `target` reports once, through the existing target-required rule. Right.** The refine returns on `''`, so no second issue is added.
6. **`tel:` is not admitted and the set was not widened. Right.** The fork clause did not fire: 9 non-test url-action sites in this repository at `df7a137923` and 8 in objectui at the old pin `9646e2ed2bf3` and at `7578323`, all admitted.
7. **CONTROL — `target` on `script` / `flow` / `modal` / `api` / `form` is untouched on both doors, and an action that never wrote `type` stays `script`. Right.** Pinned.
8. **Public surface: no new export. Right.** `packages/spec/src/ui/navigation-target.ts` is reached by relative import from `action.zod.ts` only; `ui/index.ts` does not export it; the package `exports` map is per-entry with no wildcard, so no deep path reaches it; the `api-surface` baselines are untouched in the diff. The `action-target-aliases.ts` precedent is the same shape, and #23004 can import it relatively from `view.zod.ts` without a copy.
9. **The one published-surface change is the `target` `.describe()` text, which now states the url set. Right.** It rides every schema that picks `target` from `actionObject()` — the four regenerated reference pages (`data/object`, `kernel/metadata-plugin`, `ui/action` twice, `ui/component`) are all renderings of `ActionSchema` or `InlineActionSchema`, the two doors that enforce it, so declared = enforced holds for the sentence. The TSDoc carries the full set; the describe carries the summary.
10. **D3 entry `18.ui-action-url-target-scheme-set-closed.ts`. Right.** The registry, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide are generated and never committed (#22449 B′, #22554 B; `.gitignore` lines 65–68 and 144–150), so the entry file is the whole registration and no projection needed a regeneration commit; `18` matches every sibling in `entries/semantic/`. The entry's surface and replacement match the predicate's branches, and it says the rewrite is not mechanical, which is true.
11. **Fixture triage in `action.test.ts`. Right.** The all-types loop's url arm wrote the bare `test_handler`, never a navigation target; it now writes `/test_handler` and the other arms keep their name. A test, not a producer.
12. **Generated artifacts. Right.** The four `content/docs/references/**` pages are the `gen:docs` projection of the describe; every completed Lint check-run is green.

Nothing in the diff is wrong. No governed path is touched (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green), so Prime Directive #14's tiering does not bind this landing; the record is owed because the claim declared `Clause-②` suspect on `packages/spec/src/**`.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/23010-url-action-target-scheme-set.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` **`minor`** with the **BREAKING** banner and the `!` in its title. A published accept-set narrowing is breaking (Post-Task Checklist 3: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING); it ships `minor` under the launch-window convention that `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces (a `major` is refused) and that `13458-manifest-permissions-string-list-retired.md` set as precedent with the same banner sentence. **Matches what the diff publishes.** `skip-changeset` would have been wrong: `@objectstack/spec` is a released package and its accept set moves.
- **`Clause-②:` line — `no (narrowing)` in the changeset and `no (narrowing: …)` at line start in the PR body; both read as `declared / no / narrowing`.** Clause ② asks whether a new key lands on a published payload; this diff adds no key and narrows an existing one, so `no` is the truthful value and the arm carries the breaking signal. The card body's `Clause-②: yes` was the looser reading — a bare `yes` would have declared an additive widening and lost the breaking arm — so the claim's `no (narrowing)` is right and the conflict the dev surfaced is resolved in the claim's favour.
- The migration the breaking changeset must carry is present: a FROM → TO table for every refused shape, the one-line fix, what an author now sees (`os validate`, `os build`, `defineAction`, `defineStack` refuse at `target`), and the `os migrate meta --from 17` pointer. Exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, `registered ui-action-url-target-scheme-set-closed`, resolving to the new entry file. `Check Changeset` is green on both of its runs (17:07 and 17:13).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared by the dev; none found.
- Dev deviation 1 (new module `navigation-target.ts` and the D3 entry beyond the claim's literal file list): **accepted** — the placement was delegated, the module is non-public (judgment 8), and a `registered` disposition requires the entry (judgment 10). Declared in the PR body.
- Dev deviation 2 (merged `origin/main` `c5b43b606` before opening): **accepted** — the head is the merge and every reading above is at the head.
- Dev deviation 3 (consumer runs narrowed for `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/cli`, population and blind spot declared): **accepted for the contract; convergence is CI's** — `Test Core (1–6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace` were still `in_progress` at this reading; the seat reads them before any landing act.
- Dev deviation 4 (card `Clause-②: yes` vs claim `no (narrowing)`): **answered in ②** — the claim is right.
- Dev deviation 5 (commit trailers: the repo's model-free pair, not the harness line): outside the contract; the repo's own instruction governs, so nothing to flag.
- Dev deviations 6–7 (lock contention; zero label writes): no contract content.
- Thread pointer `6123054064` (require `//` on the two web schemes so the door and the runner agree on `http:host`): **answered by the diff** — judgment 2.
- Out-of-scope findings, under Prime Directive #10: the three sibling url-target doors that admit `javascript:` today (`action:button` / `action:icon` rows, `action:group` / `action:menu` members, `DashboardHeaderActionSchema.actionUrl`, and `onSuccess.navigate`) are a declared-but-not-enforced contract gap and were **filed by the seat as #23077**, one family card — right. The `element:button` inline refusal reaching `os validate` only as a `component-props-invalid` warning is the lint props gate's own documented advisory posture, not this card's door — an acceptance note is the right carrier. `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` not restating the set is a docs nicety — acceptance note, right.
- Fork clause: not triggered, measured in both repositories (judgment 6).
- Check-runs on the head at this reading: every completed run is `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, all `Lint ·` jobs, `Type Check · source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset` ×2, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, the claim/branch/path guards, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Documentation Links`) or `skipped` by filter; `Test Core (1/6)` … `(6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace` are `in_progress`. Nothing red.
